apps.name: PS5 Pad
apps.subtitle: A direct Wi-Fi media remote for PS5
apps.localizedDescription: Control a jailbroken PS5 directly over Wi-Fi. Swipe navigation, controller buttons, Kodi playback controls and a manual live keyboard. Requires the PS5 Pad helper on the console. No Remote Play, audio/video streaming or Windows relay. Experimental software; see version notes for verified behavior and limitations.

permissions.usageDescription: PS5 Pad finds your PS5 on Wi-Fi and connects directly to its controller service. It does not stream audio or video.

versions.localizedDescription:
PS5 Pad 0.4.12 (build 18), bundled helper 2.7

The app can start its own bundled helper directly from the iPhone.
It first reuses an answering PS5 Pad helper. If absent, it sends the bundled
PS5 ELF over TCP 9021 and half-closes the write side to start it.
If the loader never accepts the connection, it falls back to Payload Manager
on HTTP 8084: check an empty private folder, upload, find the exact stored path,
and launch. A transfer that has already started never triggers a second send.

After either launch route, the app polls for a valid helper greeting and
requires helper 2.7 or newer before continuing controller initialization.
The connection menu reports the actual running helper version.
Backgrounding cancels pending work. The app never changes Payload Manager's
autoload settings, replaces elfldr, or overwrites another stored payload.
Payload Manager uses a unique uhnmeyker-ps5pad folder; after a successful
greeting it removes only that temporary upload. Failed attempts can leave that
private upload behind for inspection. There is no automatic helper upgrade
or replacement of a running controller session.

The PS5 must already be jailbroken with either its ELF loader or Payload Manager
running. No Windows bridge or PS5Upload installation is required.

Implementation references (protocol behavior, not copied upstream source):
https://github.com/phantomptr/ps5upload/blob/b30005ea499ad4ec0634e8a7ed16df1e310a6013/engine/crates/ps5upload-core/src/payload_lifecycle.rs
https://github.com/phantomptr/ps5upload/blob/b30005ea499ad4ec0634e8a7ed16df1e310a6013/engine/crates/ps5upload-core/src/payload_manager.rs

Local loader-policy/build tests and command-line console checks are separate
from the remaining on-iPhone startup test. A successful upload alone does not
prove that a helper started; a valid greeting is required.

Console verification: Payload Manager 0.6.3 accepted the exact helper bytes,
launched helper 2.7, and removed the private temporary upload after its valid
greeting. PS5 Home remained focused. No controller initialization, buttons,
power commands, autoload changes or loader replacement were sent.

PS5 Pad 0.4.11 (build 17), helper 2.7

Power Off PS5 is the bottom action in the three-dot connection menu.
It requires a connected helper 2.7 and a separate Power Off confirmation.
Cancel sends nothing. Busy or unsupported services disable the action.
This fully shuts down the PS5, closes running apps, and ends the jailbreak.
It does not enter Rest Mode or provide power-on from a fully shut-down console.

The helper calls sceShellCoreUtilRequestShutdown(2), the ShellCore request
used by StonedModder's SystemStateManager. There is no forced reboot syscall
or fallback with different semantics. API reference:
https://github.com/StonedModder/PS5-SystemStateManager/tree/414b905e285ec75ba91e48b7f908bbd6ea487ac9

The request is capability-gated, uses its own command and exact confirmation
payload, reports system errors and rejects duplicate successful requests.
The payload is an accident guard, not authentication; use a trusted LAN.
The app stops automatic reconnection on confirmation. An interrupted response
is reported as unknown; it never retries the power-off request automatically.
Service exit/update command 6 remains separate and never powers off the console.

Host tests cover confirmation, errors, duplicates, reconnect and service exit.
Actual console shutdown is deliberately left for the owner to test when ready.

Owner confirmed 0.4.10: media controls grey on Home, work in Kodi, and Kodi's
shortcut returns when Kodi closes. Existing behavior is preserved.

PS5 Pad 0.4.10 (build 16), helper 2.6

Silent Kodi media profile
The helper now reports whether Kodi is running separately from the app with
input focus. PS5 Pad checks immediately on connect and every 750 ms afterward.
Media controls enable only with fresh, confirmed Kodi focus and an initialized
controller assigned to a profile. Home, other apps, unknown/stale state and
connection loss disable and grey out the media buttons. No profile-change popup
is shown. Kodi retains the established chapter, seek and Play/Pause mappings.
VLC is no longer part of the interface; no other media mappings are guessed.

Kodi shortcut
The Kodi icon fades/shrinks away when Kodi is confirmed running, including when
Home has focus over it. It pops back when Kodi is confirmed no longer running.
Unknown/offline state does not invent a launch/exit animation; the last icon
presentation is retained, disabled. A cold launch keeps it hidden until the first
valid state arrives. Reconnecting always rechecks current state before enabling
media or the shortcut, then animates any change that happened while disconnected.
Animations use generation checks so rapid changes cannot leave the icon hidden
by an old completion handler. The icon remains in its own fixed layout slot.

Verification
Read-only probes on firmware 13.60 identified Kodi as PPSA99420. With the owner
confirming PS5 Home while Kodi remained running, the running Kodi id stayed the
same while the focused title changed to NPXS40087. Both states are distinct.
The new app/service integration and icon animations await on-phone confirmation.
No apps were launched, closed or switched by the detection tests, and no
controller input or ownership changes were used to detect application state.

Technical notes
APP_STATE is a capability-gated read-only request with a matching token and
separate known/running/focus flags. Missing replies invalidate state; delayed
responses to earlier requests and earlier network generations cannot restore it.
The PS5 APIs are read-only GetAppId / GetAppFocusedAppStatus / GetAppTitleId.
The focused status uses its first 32 bits as app id on 13.60; a generously sized
buffer accommodates the larger native response. Query errors fail closed.

PS5 Pad 0.4.9 (build 15), controller service 2.5

Controller menu
One action is shown: Initialize Controller when disconnected, or Disconnect
Controller when a virtual controller is connected. A service connection by itself
is not a controller connection. Separate Connect / Close connection entries are
removed. This includes the menu-only 0.4.8 change.

Live keyboard
The owner reported that 0.4.7 connected/disconnected a keyboard but did not type
hello. Its automatic removal after sending reports explained the short lifetime,
but the missing text's cause was not established. Do not count it as a typing pass.

Opening Keyboard now creates one temporary virtual keyboard, waits one second
before enabling the editor, then keeps it connected while the editor is active.
Text changes send live key reports. Backspace and edits within the local text are
applied by removing the changed suffix and typing its replacement. Edits queue
behind acknowledgments, so fast typing does not require one connection per key.
Enter waits for pending text, sends Enter once, releases it and removes the
keyboard. Close cancels pending typing and disconnects without pressing Enter.
The field displays only text entered in this session; it does not read the TV's
existing field or synchronize changes made with another input device.

A keyboard-specific lease is renewed every 500 ms only during the editor session.
Ordinary controller heartbeats do not keep the keyboard alive. Connection loss,
app suspension, profile takeover, controller disconnection, closing the editor or
1.8 seconds without keyboard renewal releases/removes it. Removal failure keeps
ownership for retry. The virtual controller's sleep behavior remains separate.
No typed content is written to logs, preferences or files. Text is limited to 128
printable US-ASCII characters using a US keyboard layout. Automatic detection of
the PS5 keyboard popup remains unverified and is not implemented.

Validation
Host socket tests cover persistent typing, backspace, explicit Enter, Close,
invalid input, cancellation of queued keys, client disconnect without replay,
lease expiry despite ordinary pings, and controller disconnect cleanup. Existing
ownership, initialization, protocol, input, lifecycle and discovery checks pass.
The unsigned ARM64 app was built and its USB copy verified. Service 2.5 was loaded
and its live-keyboard capability and ownership-monitor connection verified in
standby, without controller initialization, typing or media-app launch.
The owner confirmed text appears live on the TV and Close disconnects the
keyboard. USB independently verified standalone version 0.4.9, build 15.
Enter submission and the final phone menu still need owner confirmation.

No device settings, Home Screen layout or signing credentials were changed.
